solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stickler for niceties hurt in physical training

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the abbreviation for physical training

parts.note: PT is the standard abbreviation for physical training, school exercise

indicators.note: something hurt is damaged or knocked out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fussy about the finer points gets injured during a gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stickler for niceties' reads as one phrase, but 'for niceties' is the anagram fodder: 'hurt' rearranges it into ERFECTIONIS, which goes 'in' PT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact standards, which is precisely what someone demanding flawlessness does.

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A football team in China is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate. Crystal Palace is a London football club, usually just called Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal Palace, a London club, is commonly shortened to this name by fans and press.

indicators.note: a catastrophe throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lake and river rose disastrously, bringing floods.
explanation.definitionFit: A large artificial lake used to store water supply is exactly this.

indicators.note: Hemingway's first name takes in, or accepts, the single letter

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist

explanation.surface: Does Hemingway give an honest answer?
explanation.walkthrough: The surname is the misdirection: only his first name is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone serious and heartfelt, meaning what they say.

clue.text: We help in their shambolic call to vote

indicators.note: shambolic means chaotically disorganised, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A party pleads for help amid its own chaotic organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament this is the strictest instruction from party whips to attend and vote, underlined three times.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the strongest order a party whip issues to MPs to turn up and vote.

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
as is means left unaltered, in its present state

explanation.surface: Nothing changes in a desert refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot with water in the desert gives travellers a place of shelter.

indicators.note: taking the even-numbered letters in circlet, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Diamonds are set at regular intervals in a tiara.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is slang for diamonds, from their cold glitter.

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A teetotaller caught up in a quarrel makes people giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests an argument; here it is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a nervous suppressed laugh, much like a giggle.

clue.text: Large ears reshaped in surgical beam

parts.note: L is the usual clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: reshaping the word ears gives its letters a new form and order

explanation.surface: Big ears are surgically remodelled using a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons use focused light beams of this kind to cut or seal tissue precisely.

clue.text: On piano in group to admire

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the letter for piano is placed inside the word for group

parts.note: a sect is a group with shared beliefs
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pianist performing within an ensemble wins admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high regard is to esteem them; the verb phrase matches the infinitive.

clue.text: Get wheels in middle for train

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for middle

parts.note: the core is the middle of something

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn about, so the letters of Get spin round into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to fetch wheels for the centre of a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway train; here it is a procession. 'wheels' makes TEG from Get, which goes 'in' CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral procession trailing behind a hearse is a train of mourners.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, the unit of time
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A sequel or second tale turns out to be dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer fresh or interesting is tired and dull, as with an over-familiar joke.

clue.text: Say A380 flying near a Pole

indicators.note: letters flying about land in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An Airbus A380 jet flies close to the North or South Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the A380 as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airbus A380 is a large airliner, an example of a passenger aircraft.

clue.text: Boat from Oxford University set off

parts.note: to trigger something is to set it off

explanation.surface: A boat leaves from Oxford University, perhaps for a rowing race.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a canoe-type vessel steadied by a float on a projecting frame, a type of boat.

parts.note: to gall someone is to vex or irritate them
an ant is an insect with six legs, so a six-footer

explanation.surface: A courageous man annoys a very tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashing, chivalrous young man is a gallant, typically bold and courageous.

indicators.note: the word for also cuts into the word for dash, splitting it

parts.note: a dash is a small amount, a bit
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A thief also slashing at someone in a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' suggests a sprint; it is a dash of something, a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw who robs travellers, often armed, is a robber.

indicators.note: turned round, the combined words are read backwards

parts.note: a slip is a lapse or error, a sin
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A cricket slip catch turned the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip catch' is a cricket term (a catch by a fielder beside the wicketkeeper), but here the words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, one of many games.

clue.text: Arterial route in Australia or Tasmania

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of letters across Australia or Tasmania

explanation.surface: A main road in Australia or its island state of Tasmania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arterial route' suggests a main road; it is the body's chief artery, sitting 'in' AustraliA OR TAsmania.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest artery carries blood from the heart, literally the body's main arterial route.

indicators.note: the article holds the untruth inside it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lie is an untruth

explanation.surface: A foreign newspaper article contains a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means strange or from another country.

clue.text: Draw attention from cuts in English energy

indicators.note: the word for cuts is set between the two single letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
clips are cuts, as when trimming hair

explanation.surface: Someone draws attention away from spending cuts in English energy policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine or overshadow something is to divert notice from it, as the moon blocks the sun.

indicators.note: the dish surrounds, or circles, the jumbled letters

parts.note: a dish is a vessel for food

indicators.note: swirling fog moves about, so its letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A shark-hunting boat goes round and round in thick swirling fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a dish; 'swirling' makes OGF from fog, which DISH 'circles'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small shark of coastal waters, also sold as rock salmon, is a species of shark.

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a goal is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An instruction to state your purpose briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb; it is an Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small state on India's west coast.

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of heavy cast-iron cooking stove
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: The stove at home is playing up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a large British range cooker, a fixture of country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a further time, a repeat of what happened before.

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
potters are the class of people who make ceramics

explanation.surface: A tutor runs a pottery class for nerdy types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' suggests a lesson, but here it is a category of people: those who throw pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbyists who log locomotive numbers are the stock British image of obsessive nerds.
